questions.question: Write a note on approaches to OB
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Organizational Behaviour (OB) relies on four foundational approaches to
  • understand workplace dynamics
  •  Human Resources (Supportive) Approach: Focuses on employee growth
  • and development, believing that nurturing talent naturally leads to better
  • performance.
  •  Contingency Approach: Rejects a "one-size-fits-all" management style
  • arguing that different situational variables require unique leadership
  • responses.
  •  Productivity Approach: Evaluates the efficiency of inputs transforming into
  • high-quality outputs, balancing economic value with employee satisfaction.
  •  Systems Approach: Views the organization as a complex, interrelated set of
  • variables where individual, group, and structural actions continuously
  • influence one another.
questions.final_answer: influence one another
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Founders’ Values and Vision plays a significant role in shaping Founders’ / Values and Vision. Explain
questions.solution_html:
• Founders’ Values and Vision plays a significant role in shaping
  • Organisational Culture. Explain
  • Ans: Founders are the ultimate architects of an organization's initial culture.
  • Because they start with a clean slate, their personal values, beliefs, and vision drive
  • early decision-making, hiring criteria, and operational goals. Founders typically
  • recruit individuals who share their mindset, socializing them into specific ways of
  • thinking and behaving.
  • Furthermore, the founders’ early successes establish "the right way to do things,"
  • turning their personal philosophies into institutional norms. Over time, these values
  • become deeply embedded in the organizational fabric, persisting as a defining
  • cultural legacy long after the founders have stepped away from daily operations.
questions.final_answer: cultural legacy long after the founders have stepped away from daily operations
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the role of specialisation and departmentalisation in Organisational / Culture
questions.solution_html:
• Structure
  • Ans: While work specialization and departmentalization are classic building blocks of
  • organizational structure, they also play a profound, quiet role in shaping a company's

  • how they interact, what they value, and how they perceive their workplace identity.

  • social dynamics

  • B. Departmentalization and Culture: Departmentalization (how specialized jobs

  • boundaries and cultural subcultures
  •  The Rise of Subcultures
  •  The "Silo Mentality" Risk
  •  Cross-Functional Integration

questions.question: Differnetiate between functional and cross functional team
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Functional and cross-functional teams differ primarily in their structural
  • composition and operational goals
  •  Functional Teams: Comprise a manager and subordinates from the same
  • specialized department, such as accounting or human resources. They focus
  • on routine, ongoing vertical tasks within their specific discipline, featuring a
  • clear, traditional hierarchy.
  •  Cross-Functional Teams: Bring together experts from diverse departments
  • (e.g., marketing, R&D, and production) to collaborate on a specific project or
  • solve a unique problem. They operate horizontally, breaking down
  • departmental silos to foster innovation, speed up decision-making, and offer
  • diverse perspectives that a single functional unit cannot provide.
questions.final_answer: diverse perspectives that a single functional unit cannot provide
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: An individual's perception is influenced by his cultural and social background. / Explain
questions.solution_html:
• An individual's perception is influenced by his cultural and social
  • background. Explain
  • Ans: Perception is not a passive recording of reality; it is an active process of
  • interpreting sensory input, heavily filtered by an individual's cultural and social
  • upbringing. Cultural background instills specific values, beliefs, and behavioral norms
  • that dictate what a person attends to or ignores. Similarly, social background—
  • including education, social class, and peer groups—shapes personal expectations
  • and biases.
  • When facing an ambiguous situation at work, two employees will interpret the exact
  • same event differently because their unique background filters cause them to assign
  • meaning based on what their specific culture deems important or acceptable.
questions.final_answer: meaning based on what their specific culture deems important or acceptable
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Group cohesion improves team performance. Elaborate
questions.solution_html:
• Group cohesion improves team performance. Elaborate
  • Ans: Group cohesion—the degree to which members are motivated to stay in a
  • team and align with its goals—acts as a powerful performance multiplier. In highly
  • cohesive teams, members share a strong sense of belonging, which naturally fosters
  • open communication, mutual trust, and a willingness to help colleagues overcome
  • bottlenecks. This alignment minimizes interpersonal friction and destructive conflict
  • allowing the team to channel its collective energy into productivity.
  • Furthermore, high cohesion boosts individual morale and commitment, which
  • significantly reduces absenteeism and inspires members to readily accept
  • accountability to avoid letting their teammates down.
questions.final_answer: accountability to avoid letting their teammates down
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Differnetiate between functional and cross functional team
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Functional and cross-functional teams differ primarily in their structural
  • composition and operational goals
  •  Functional Teams: Comprise a manager and subordinates from the same
  • specialized department, such as accounting or human resources. They focus
  • on routine, ongoing vertical tasks within their specific discipline, featuring a
  • clear, traditional hierarchy.
  •  Cross-Functional Teams: Bring together experts from diverse departments
  • (e.g., marketing, R&D, and production) to collaborate on a specific project or
  • solve a unique problem. They operate horizontally, breaking down
  • departmental silos to foster innovation, speed up decision-making, and offer
  • diverse perspectives that a single functional unit cannot provide.

questions.question: An individual's perception is influenced by his cultural and social background. / Explain
questions.solution_html:
• An individual's perception is influenced by his cultural and social
  • background. Explain
  • Ans: Perception is not a passive recording of reality; it is an active process of
  • interpreting sensory input, heavily filtered by an individual's cultural and social
  • upbringing. Cultural background instills specific values, beliefs, and behavioral norms
  • that dictate what a person attends to or ignores. Similarly, social background—
  • including education, social class, and peer groups—shapes personal expectations
  • and biases.
  • When facing an ambiguous situation at work, two employees will interpret the exact
  • same event differently because their unique background filters cause them to assign
  • meaning based on what their specific culture deems important or acceptable.
questions.final_answer: meaning based on what their specific culture deems important or acceptable

questions.question: Group cohesion improves team performance. Elaborate
questions.solution_html:
• Group cohesion improves team performance. Elaborate
  • Ans: Group cohesion—the degree to which members are motivated to stay in a
  • team and align with its goals—acts as a powerful performance multiplier. In highly
  • cohesive teams, members share a strong sense of belonging, which naturally fosters
  • open communication, mutual trust, and a willingness to help colleagues overcome
  • bottlenecks. This alignment minimizes interpersonal friction and destructive conflict
  • allowing the team to channel its collective energy into productivity.
  • Furthermore, high cohesion boosts individual morale and commitment, which
  • significantly reduces absenteeism and inspires members to readily accept
  • accountability to avoid letting their teammates down.
questions.final_answer: accountability to avoid letting their teammates down
